title: Training, validation and clustering
subtitle: How do you know a model works? Hide some data, test on it — and learn what to do when there are no labels at all.

types.title: Supervised and unsupervised
types.body: Supervised: examples come with answers (labels) — regression, classification. Unsupervised: no labels; find structure — clustering, dimensionality reduction. Reinforcement: learn from reward by acting.

perc.title: A learning loop: the perceptron
perc.body: A perceptron predicts sign(w·x + b). For every mistake, nudge the weights toward the correct class: w ← w + η·y·x. On separable data it converges: here in 6 epochs to w = (1, 0.5), b = -1. Training is this loop: predict, measure error, adjust.

split.title: Train / validation / test
split.body: Judging a model on the data it trained on rewards memorising. Split: train (fit, e.g. 70 %), validation (choose settings, 15 %), test (final unbiased score, 15 %, used once). k-fold cross-validation rotates the validation part k times and averages — good for small data.
split.steps: 1000 rows split 70 / 15 / 15. That is 700 training, 150 validation, 150 test rows.

conf.title: Classification metrics
conf.body: Confusion matrix: TP, FP, FN, TN. Accuracy = (TP + TN)/all; precision = TP/(TP + FP); recall = TP/(TP + FN); F1 is their harmonic mean. With rare positives accuracy is deceiving.
conf.steps: TP = 8, FP = 2, FN = 4, TN = 86. Precision = 8/10 = 0.8; recall = 8/12 = 0.67; accuracy = 94/100.

km.title: k-means clustering
km.body: Pick k centroids; assign each point to the nearest; move each centroid to its cluster mean; repeat until stable. On the sample data it stops in 3 iterations with centroids (1.25,1.5) (3.9,5.1) and within-cluster SSE 8.525. Choose k with the “elbow” of SSE vs k.

bv.title: Bias–variance
bv.body: Too simple a model is biased (underfits: high error everywhere). Too flexible a model has high variance (overfits: low train, high test error). The best model sits between. More data reduces variance; better features reduce bias.
